title: Independently check the mixed-rank rare-tag batching step
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

The exact Cartesian line count gives at least W^(m−1) jobs for a flag/axis class under the common-page and support conditions. Current-value flag scheduling then equals the original sparse-axis order. A two-axis width-four request with only two lines shows the need for the eventual-size condition.

## Task and overlap

Scoped #7852 follow-up at `41beda1d6435760dc99e38bd7e65f36798aad212` on main `e54523517d0f03e58352e647c403a5af3e525a57`. This is an independent scoped review of #7846 at `343f7b1817e26ad3f89d2ddad313b12741d53602`, which already states the batching step for #7830’s 480-factor application at `87fbf4f7b35b0f18ab12b5767775a9a424cf0b15`. It examines current-value and full-batch obligations only.

## Validation

`python3 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/p104-rare-tag-batch-check` and the committed-byte check passed on CPython 3.12.3. The separately written oracle checks all 15,625 coefficients on a 5×5×5 core. Stale-source, cross-support and underfilled-batch controls are rejected. Actual Gaussian page layout and physical transfer remain to be rebound.

## Credit

Credit Ali Romman for the submitted uniform construction and grouped Gaussian step. Clear1nsight prepared this package with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance.

## Open next questions

Bind page support and time-ordered current values to the literal routed Gaussian execution.
